name: Homocysteine
rangeNote: No single range is used, because suggested limits differ between sources and labs (for example, risk was described as rising from about 10 µmol/L and levels above 12 µmol/L as moderately raised in a German-Austrian-Swiss consensus, and above 11 µmol/L in older adults in a dementia consensus). Levels rise if the blood sample is left unspun before it reaches the lab. Folate, vitamin B12 and vitamin B6 supplements can lower the level.
summary: Homocysteine is an amino acid the body makes when it processes methionine, a protein building block. B vitamins (folate, B12 and B6) help clear it, so the level partly reflects their status and kidney function.

high.meaning: A raised homocysteine is linked in studies to a higher chance of cardiovascular disease and, in older adults, to cognitive decline. It is read as a pointer to B vitamin status or kidney function; whether lowering it prevents these conditions is a separate question that trials have not settled.
commonCauses: Low folate, vitamin B12 or vitamin B6
Metformin (associated with lower B12 and higher homocysteine)
Smoking, heavy alcohol or coffee intake

low.meaning: A low homocysteine is generally not a concern. It is common in people who take B vitamin supplements or eat plenty of folate-rich foods.
